slides.label: HOOK
title: Per finished video hour.
slides.vo: Ten euros. Per hour of finished video — edited, captioned, ready to post. The market charges around fifty euros an hour for editing. Why the gap? … Not by cutting quality — by changing how the work gets made. Give me two minutes and you'll know if this is for you.

slides.label: PROBLEM
title: You post late.
Because of editing.
bullets: First cut lands in 3 to 5 days
slides.vo: You get the idea on Monday. The footage goes out Tuesday. The first cut comes back Friday. One revision, and you are three days behind again. Meanwhile the algorithm rewarded someone else — the person who actually published.

slides.label: COST
title: Waiting costs
more than editing.
slides.vo: Editing is not the real cost. The real cost? … the week with no video. The subscription you keep paying while the file still does not exist. The freelancer at fifty euros an hour you are now afraid to call.

slides.label: MECHANISM
title: I sell the result.
Not the tool.
slides.vo: Nothing here is a subscription. You do not learn software, you do not configure anything, you do not watch a single tutorial. You send your footage, you receive the finished video. The tool I use is my problem — the result is yours.

slides.label: PROOF
title: 1M+ views.
On my own posts.
slides.vo: Over a million views across all my own posts. The Instagram screenshots are on the page, not in a deck. Open them, count them: the work speaks, not a promise.

slides.label: PRICE
title: €50/h → €10/h.
Of finished video.
bullets: Billed on delivered hours, not my time
slides.vo: The price: … ten euros per hour of finished video. Not ten euros of my time — ten euros of what you receive. You pay for the file, not for a contractor's invoice.

slides.label: PROCESS
title: 3 steps.
Zero meetings.
slides.vo: One scene, three moves. You send your footage and your intent — one sentence is enough. I edit, I caption, I cut it for the platform. You get the file, you publish. No meeting, no discovery call, no endless quote.

slides.label: FORMATS
title: Captions.
slides.vo: What you get: the vertical version for Reels and Shorts, the wide version for YouTube, burned-in captions for everyone watching without sound, and a timestamped chapter list, ready to paste under your video.

slides.label: OBJECTION
title: "Is this just
one AI button?"
slides.vo: No. This is not a prompt you fire and a video comes back. There is a brief, a human doing the edit, and an approval before delivery. The accelerator is artificial; the responsibility is not.

slides.label: TURNAROUND
title: The deadline
comes before the payment.
bullets: Said no when I can't hold it
slides.vo: Timelines are announced before you pay for anything: a short video usually ships the same day, steady volume gets a reserved slot. And if I cannot hold a deadline, I say so before I take your footage.

slides.label: WHO IT'S FOR
title: Creators, brands,
agencies.
bullets: They want a price per result
slides.vo: Who this is for: the creator who publishes every week and loses evenings to editing; the e-commerce brand that needs ten variations a month; the agency reselling video to its clients without hiring another editor.

slides.label: CTA
title: Send footage.
Get a video.
bullets: The link is under this video
slides.vo: The best judgement is the trial. Send me a clip: you get thirty seconds of edited video, free, before any commitment. Then you decide. The link is under the video.
